column4: A mutex needs a unique, sendable payload; its callback must hold no authority and return sendable data.
column5: help: Build a unique payload before `mutex.create` and pass its ownership with `take value`. Keep `mutex.with` callbacks `uses {}`; perform I/O and synchronization outside them.

column4: A channel payload must be owned and sendable. A Receiver cannot be part of a channel payload.
column5: help: Pass an owned sendable value with `take value` at its last use. For copyable counted data, `unique value` can remove sharing when allocation is permitted. Remove local borrows and Receiver parts from the payload.

column4: No arm of the enclosing error type has exactly one field whose type is the propagated nominal error. The diagnostic offers three repairs; only the first is a mechanical edit, and its JSON `fix` appends the arm to a declaration in the same file. When the error type is serializable, a note says that the arm changes its stored and wire schema (STORE-7, SER-2).
column5: help: (a) Add the arm the fix proposes, such as `File(FileError)`; this changes the error contract of every function returning the type, so prefer it only when callers should see that failure. (b) Handle the error at the site with `match` or `let Ok(..) = .. else { .. }`. (c) Map it explicitly with `? C`, a function from the propagated error or an arm whose payload it is.

column4: Two or more arms of the enclosing error type carry the propagated error. Each is a different role, such as `Storage(StoreError)` and `Unknown(StoreError)`, so plain `?` chooses none and there is no automatic fix.
column5: help: Name the arm whose role fits this site: `? Storage` or `? Unknown`.

column4: Plain `?` injects only nominal errors: a named type or a type parameter. A `String`, `Bytes` or other primitive, tuple, function or builtin error names no error domain.
column5: help: Name the arm that carries it, such as `? Utf8` for a `Bytes` error, or map it with a function.

column4: No body of the package constructs this arm of one of its package-private error types, so callers match a failure that never happens. `pub` types are not linted, since other packages can construct their arms.
column5: help: Remove the arm if nothing fails that way any more, updating the matches that name it, or construct it where that failure occurs.

column4: Freezing requires a unique, inert graph containing no resources. Freeze and thaw may allocate.
column5: help: Make copyable counted data unique before `shared.freeze`, and remove resource or authority-bearing parts. `copy value` shares storage and cannot prove uniqueness. An existing Shared root is copied with `copy`; recovering its unique contents requires `shared.thaw`.

column4: Resources, task handles, Receivers, once closures, arenas, regions and values containing them can only be moved or borrowed.
column5: help: Borrow the value when the callee only reads it. To transfer an owned value at its last use, write `take value`; change a borrowed parameter to a `take` parameter if the function must consume it. `copy value` cannot repair a noncopyable type.
